problem.text: The chat example lacked a command-line switch to suppress generation of reasoning delimiters.

reasoning.text: The patch reuses Job.banned_strings rather than removing tags from displayed output. This constrains generated text, not whether a model produces reasoning without delimiters.

impact.text: The accompanying streaming-call change is incompatible with both existing console implementations and affects chat even when --no_think is absent.

source_notes.text: PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example,” proposes an API endpoint and discusses prompt-template integration and problematic model output. Its relationship here is only inferred from its explicit examples/chat.py usage and reasoning-mode discussion; it does not establish the motivation for this patch.

limitations: No model generation, native banned-string matching, or interactive console session was executed. The bounded Python check validates argument binding only.

claims.text: The new -no_think/--no_think store_true option selects [tt[0], tt[1]] as each response job's banned strings; otherwise the job receives None. tt is obtained once per response from prompt_format.thinktag().

The base template returns <think> and </think>; the alternative override returns an opening string containing a leading space and trailing newline, ' <reasoning>\n', and </reasoning>. The patch passes these strings unchanged rather than normalizing delimiter whitespace.

Job lowercases banned strings and prepares UTF-32 matching buffers. Its output path checks lowercased held text, retains a checkpoint for partial matches, and rewinds on completed matches while reporting suppressed text and tokens. This is generation-side suppression, unlike stop strings, whose matching branch terminates the response.

--think remains independent: it still appends the opening delimiter to the input prompt. --no_think neither removes that prompt text nor disables --think; the new help explicitly cautions that suppressing tags need not prevent reasoning.

A standard-library check extracted both console method signatures and tested argument binding. The parent call shape was accepted for both; the patched call shape failed with 'too many positional arguments'.

findings.description: The updated chat loop passes both delimiters to stream(), but neither console method accepts the additional argument.
findings.trigger: Any generator result reaches s.stream(chunk, tt[0], tt[1]) in examples/chat.py, in either basic or rich console mode, regardless of --no_think.
findings.expected_behavior: The selected console consumes the generated chunk and continues the response loop.
findings.actual_behavior: Argument binding raises TypeError before the stream method body runs. The whole-parent search found the chat loop as the only matching Python console .stream call; this observation concerns the interactive example, not all Generator users.

verification.description: Compared the changed call with both unchanged stream signatures and inspected console selection and the whole-parent call search.
Extracted method parameters using ast and modeled parent and patched positional calls with inspect.Signature.bind.
verification.limits: Tests Python argument compatibility, not repository method execution or GPU generation.

annotation.summary: Adds optional generation-side suppression of reasoning tags, but also introduces a stream-call argument mismatch affecting both chat console modes.
